events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $5.77 (model confidence 0.70)
events.body:
Both advocates requested no_action and neither raised a supported ground; the record itself shows an off-route segment. [F3] establishes one off-route segment 18:50–19:00 driving 6.93 km where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, adding 4.09 km; under RD-1 an unexplained deviation violates the driver's shortest-and-most-direct obligation. [F3][RD-1]

RD-4 does not excuse it: the trace shows ✗ RD-4(a) — no traffic incident on the replaced stretch (F15 records none), and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment (RD-4(b), MVP practice). [F12][F15][RD-4]

The decisive question is consent under RD-5. The driver's message at 18:46 asked a SPECIFIC route: "ok if I go round via Defu Avenue 1?" [F8], and the rider's reply at 18:47, "Can lah, go ahead," is a clear agreement [F9], sent before the segment started at 18:50:10 and captured in a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10]. Read in context, the rider agreed to the driver's named road, not to a general free choice of route — the driver's later statement "the rider said can" [F11] is only a claim of verbal agreement and would not itself be consent (G11), but the chat already shows it. [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]

Scope is where the agreement falls short. A specific named-road agreement ("go round via Defu Avenue 1") covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road. [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5][G13]

Because the trace states this question cannot be answered and that nothing establishes the exemption, and because the skipped element is the missing path-to-road link (a record that a clause needs), the segment is the unexempted one. [F3][RD-1][RD-5][G13]

The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres enter the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch applies. The skipped link short-changes the driver's excuse rather than stripping proof of a charge, and the code has measured the extra distance, so the amount is computable: 4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.7669, rounded to $5.77. [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]

Ordinary cab charges stay: the $0.11 waiting fee matches 0.4 min × $0.26/min [F5], there is no surge [F6], and no unexempted ERP/undisclosed item appears in the total [F7], so no FARE-1 or FARE-2 adjustment is available. [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1][FARE-2]

The complaint only queries whether the fare was high and whether the stated road was the one driven; the messages are an agreed route change. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears. 18:46, 18:47, complaint text. [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]

RIDER: We reviewed your fare dispute. The fare was mostly correct, but part of your trip went off the shortest route: for about 10 minutes you were driven 6.93 km where the direct route is 2.84 km, adding 4.09 km. You did agree to a route change by chat, but only for one named road, and the record doesn't show the car actually went that way, so that stretch isn't covered by your agreement. We're refunding the extra $5.77 as a Ryde voucher. Ordinary metered charges stay. No action against your account.

Your passenger agreed by chat to go via the road you named, but that agreement only covered that named road, and the record doesn't show the driven route was on it, so the segment isn't exempt. This is a metered trip, so the extra $5.77 in distance is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. No account flag: you have no prior upheld route disputes.

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts.
